defects.summary: golden_sound_events() takes segments[0] (_event_from_row, perception_test.py:172-190) as each acoustic row's ground-truth event. For both rows in the golden `perception-test-acoustic` track (video_8241, video_9253) segment 0 is labelled 'Muted' — the annotators' marker for a stretch with NO audible source. label_phrase then renders it as 'right now there is an audible muted sound or event', so the track's recall / fusion_fp / recall_flip metrics would be scored against SILENCE. The valid-split annotations carry no 'Muted' label, so only the checked-in train-split sample.json rows are affected — which is exactly what the golden manifest pins. This corpus filters NON_SOUND_LABELS instead.

AcousticOnset's shipped thresholds (high=0.09, low=0.0225) are mean-square ENERGY, and no capture chunk in 40 annotated clips (3973 chunks, 987s) reaches 0.09: corpus max energy is 0.0277. run(audio_gate='acoustic-onset') with default audio_wake therefore NEVER admits on this material — an audio Watch is silently deaf, with no health event to say so.
defects.repro: eval/stage-validation/sv_audio.py --only SV-A1.6R (check: 'the SHIPPED audio gate admits at least one annotated sound event')

defects.summary: EnergyVad's defaults are dimensionless FRAME counts (hangover_frames=8, min_speech_frames=3) ported from percept-edge/src/vad.js, but the Python runtime feeds it capture chunks of AudioSourceConfig.chunk_s=0.25s (percept/runtime/audio.py:56). The effective hangover is therefore 2.00s of CONTINUOUS silence and the minimum utterance 0.75s. Combined with utterance_threshold=0.01 arriving as energy 1e-4, continuous narration reads as one unbroken speech run and endpoints essentially never — the saturation observed on omnipro, reproduced here.

In the compiled audio-only path, a unit arriving while muted()/paused() is `continue`d with no counter increment and no RuntimeHealthEvent. 5 of 14 units offered in this run are therefore invisible: RuntimeStats has no audio-suppressed field (only frames_dropped, which is the video path), SourceTracker never sees them (runtime_ended source_coverage reports excluded=0), and no health event names them. Units in != admitted + suppressed + dropped-with-receipt: the suppressed term has no term.
defects.repro: eval/stage-validation/sv_audio.py --only SV-A4.8 (check: 'the end-of-run coverage report accounts for every unit offered')

defects.summary: prepare_audio_judge_binding accepts only an exact percept.backends.fake.FakeVision or percept.backends.gemini.GeminiVision instance, so a JudgePool — including one whose JudgeCapability explicitly declares the 'audio' and 'fused' evidence shapes (percept/backends/judge_pool.py:35) — is rejected and apply_watch_plan returns 'rejected'. The compiled audio path therefore never inherits the pool's per-route capacity (max_inflight), latency SLO/deadline, hedging or JudgeRouteReceipts. It is NOT unbounded: the byte caps, the AudioWindow caps and the default judge_dispatch='async' single-flight scheduler bound it — but the bound is the runtime's, not the pool's, and there is no receipt trail per route.

notes: Recall is scored against the ANY-SOUND ground truth (every annotated sound segment in the clip, merged): an energy-threshold gate cannot distinguish one sound label from another, so scoring it against a single label would measure the wrong thing. Label-specific recall at the same operating point is reported beside it.
An admission counts as a hit when a wake instant lands within 0.25s of the annotated interval — one capture chunk, because an onset is reported at the chunk's END.
No default is proposed. The frontier is reported; picking an operating point needs a consequence model (miss cost vs. spend) this suite does not have.

The speech slice is SMALL — 3 case(s), 400s. The local OmniPro media is the benchmark's VISUAL subset (19 of 245 videos), so only a handful of rows with an audio-carried trigger have media on disk. Read the endpoint counts as an order of magnitude, not a rate; the speech-fraction column is the load-bearing measurement and it is stable across the slice.
